authoredNote: Expectations written from the Svelte 5 rule that a keyed `{#each xs as b (K)}` binds `b` and evaluates `K`, and from the grammar's own shape (probed: `each_start` carries TWO `svelte_raw_text` fragments — the collection, then `b` or `b (K)` — so a rule that splits on the first `(` is reading the grammar, not guessing). Line pins read off the post-fix run and checked against the fixture's text: `(sortKey)` on 39, `{id}` on 50, the unkeyed collection on 53.
rationale: JOB 2 of the svelte ontology pass. The keyed each form's KEY was never read, and its property leaves were registered as TEMPLATE-LOCAL SHADOWS. Corpus measurement: the keyed form occurs 699 times in 486 of the 6,439 .svelte files. Two defects in one rule: `{#each todos as todo (todo.id)}` silenced a member named `id` for the whole block (pinned below as the `id` read on line 50), and `{#each rows as row (keyOf(row))}` published `uses rows` and nothing for `keyOf`. The head is the binding list and the parenthesised tail is a READ on the same S1 argument as the collection. The collector's own dot rule keeps the ordinary keyed block `{#each rows as row (row.id)}` silent at `id`, which is pinned so a future widening cannot publish the most common false edge there is. The unkeyed control `{#each rows as row, i}` on line 53 is the regression stop: a rule that collected the whole fragment as reads would publish the bindings `row` and `i`, and the forbids catch exactly that.

forbidRelationships.comment: the each BINDING is a template-local, never a member read. The pre-fix rule and a naive whole-fragment collector both publish it.
the second each binding is a template-local too — the S5 shadow case, and the control for the unkeyed form on line 53
`row.n` is a member LEAF on a binding; the collector's dot rule skips it, so no component-level read of `n` is derivable

`{#each rows as row (row.id)}` on line 49 contributes NO read of a member named `id` — the key's leaf belongs to the binding. The member read of `id` on line 50 is a separate fact and is pinned above; if the rule published the key's leaf this forbid would fire on the wrong target.
